sections.title: Music Therapy
sections.intro: Music Therapy uses purposeful musical experiences to work toward therapeutic goals. Sessions can support communication, emotional expression, regulation, attention, movement and social connection in an engaging and strengths-based way.

sections.title: Support built around everyday participation.
sections.intro: Therapy goals are individual. These examples show common areas that may be explored when they are relevant to the person and their priorities.

items.title: Communication
items.description: Using rhythm, songs and musical interaction to encourage expressive and receptive communication.

items.title: Emotional expression
items.description: Creating safe ways to identify, express and explore emotions.

items.title: Regulation
items.description: Using predictable musical experiences to support calm, engagement and transitions.

items.title: Social connection
items.description: Shared music-making can encourage turn-taking, joint attention and connection.

items.title: Attention & participation
items.description: Structured musical activities can support focus, motivation and active participation.

items.title: Movement
items.description: Rhythm and music can be used to encourage coordinated movement and body awareness.

panels.title: A clear, practical pathway.
checks: Collaboration with family and other supports

panels.title: Goals first, service second.
paragraphs: Music Therapy can be adapted to different ages, communication styles and support needs where the service is clinically suitable.
We start by understanding what is working well, what feels difficult and what meaningful change would look like in daily life. From there, the clinician can recommend a suitable next step.

items.title: Start with your priorities
items.description: Tell us what matters, what is currently difficult and what you hope to change.

items.title: Understand strengths & needs
items.description: Your clinician gathers relevant information and completes assessment where appropriate.

items.title: Build practical strategies
items.description: Sessions focus on meaningful goals and strategies that make sense in real routines.

items.title: Review & adapt
items.description: Progress is reviewed together and the plan is adjusted as needs and goals change.

sections.title: Before you get started.
sections.intro: These answers are general. We can discuss individual circumstances when you contact the team.

items.question: Do I need musical skills?
items.answer: No. Music Therapy is not a music lesson and does not require prior musical ability.

items.question: What can happen in a session?
items.answer: Sessions may include singing, instruments, rhythm, movement, improvisation or listening activities selected to support specific goals.

items.question: Can Music Therapy complement other therapies?
items.answer: Yes. Where appropriate, goals can be coordinated with other allied health supports.
